title: At the café
summary: Order drinks politely with أُرِيدُ and 'please', and say whether a drink is hot or cold.
intro: To order, say what you want with أُرِيدُ (I want, I'd like) and add 'please': مِنْ فَضْلِكَ to a man, مِنْ فَضْلِكِ to a woman. The drink is the object, so it takes -an, as you learned yesterday: أُرِيدُ شَايًا. A cup of something is فِنْجَان + the drink: فِنْجَانُ قَهْوَة.
objectives: Order a drink with أُرِيدُ and مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
Ask a café what it has with هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ…؟
Say that a drink is hot or cold, for a masculine and a feminine noun
Say how sweet you want your coffee

realLife.title: A hot afternoon
realLife.story: After class it is hot, and Sami takes Daniel and Layla to an old café near the school. Layla knows exactly how she likes her coffee, Daniel wants anything cold, and Sami orders hot tea, as Egyptians do in any weather. When the bill comes, Sami will not let anyone else pay.

sentences.en: I'd like a cup of coffee, please. (to a man)
sentences.literal: I want a cup (of) coffee, from your kindness

mistakes.why: The container comes first: 'a cup of coffee' is finjān qahwa, literally 'cup (of) coffee'.

segs: you have (to several people; lit. at you)

sentences.en: The water is cold and the coffee is hot.
sentences.literal: the water (is) cold and the coffee (is) hot

mistakes.why: qahwa is feminine (it ends in ة), so the adjective takes ة too.

sentences.literal: what do you want, O Layla

mistakes.why: Speaking to a woman, the verb ends in -īna: turīdīna. turīdu is for a man.

sentences.ar: أُرِيدُ شَايًا بِدُونِ سُكَّر، لَوْ سَمَحْتِ.
sentences.en: I'd like a tea without sugar, please. (to a woman)
sentences.literal: I want tea without sugar, if you allow

dialogue.title: Hot tea on a hot day
dialogue.culture: In an Egyptian café you say how sweet your coffee should be: سَادَة (no sugar), مَضْبُوط (medium) or زِيَادَة (extra sweet). Waiters often call a male customer يَا أُسْتَاذ (sir). Friends argue politely over who pays; الْحِسَاب عَلَيَّ means 'the bill is on me'.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر وَأَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا! تَفَضَّلُوا، هٰذِهِ طَاوِلَة جَمِيلَة.
lines.en: Good afternoon and welcome! Please sit down, here is a nice table.
segs: please, come in, sit down (to several people)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا! يَا دَانْيَال، هٰذَا مَقْهىً قَدِيم وَمَشْهُور فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
lines.en: Thank you! Daniel, this is an old and famous café in Cairo.

lines.ar: مَاذَا تَشْرَبُونَ؟ عِنْدَنَا شَايْ وَقَهْوَة وَعَصِير طَازَج.
lines.en: What will you drink? We have tea, coffee and fresh juice.

lines.ar: أُرِيدُ فِنْجَانَ قَهْوَة تُرْكِيَّة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: I'd like a cup of Turkish coffee, please.

lines.ar: حَاضِر! كَيْفَ تُرِيدِينَ الْقَهْوَةَ؟ سَادَة أَمْ مَضْبُوط أَمْ زِيَادَة؟
lines.en: Certainly! How would you like the coffee? No sugar, medium or extra sweet?

lines.ar: مَضْبُوط، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. أُرِيدُ قَلِيلًا مِنَ السُّكَّر فَقَطْ.
lines.en: Medium, please. I only want a little sugar.

lines.ar: وَأَنْتَ يَا أُسْتَاذ؟ مَاذَا تُرِيدُ؟ شَايًا أَمْ قَهْوَةً؟
lines.en: And you, sir? What would you like? Tea or coffee?

lines.ar: الْجَوّ حَارّ جِدًّا الْيَوْم! أُرِيدُ شَيْئًا بَارِدًا، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ.
lines.en: The weather is very hot today! I'd like something cold, please.

lines.ar: عِنْدَنَا عَصِير لَيْمُون بِالنَّعْنَاع، بَارِد وَلَذِيذ جِدًّا.
lines.en: We have lemon juice with mint, cold and really delicious.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز! أُرِيدُ عَصِيرَ لَيْمُون، وَزُجَاجَةَ مَاء بَارِد أَيْضًا.
lines.en: Excellent! I'd like a lemon juice, and a bottle of cold water too.

lines.ar: وَأَنَا أُرِيدُ شَايًا سَاخِنًا بِالْحَلِيب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: And I would like a hot tea with milk, please.

lines.ar: شَايْ سَاخِن الْآن؟ لٰكِنَّ الْجَوّ حَارّ جِدًّا يَا سَامِي!
lines.en: Hot tea now? But the weather is so hot, Sami!

lines.ar: فِي مِصْر نَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ السَّاخِنَ فِي كُلِّ وَقْت!
lines.en: In Egypt we drink hot tea at any time of day!

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلُوا: الْقَهْوَة وَالشَّايْ وَالْعَصِير وَالْمَاء. بِالْهَنَاء!
lines.en: Here you are: the coffee, the tea, the juice and the water. Enjoy!

lines.ar: الْعَصِير لَذِيذ جِدًّا! يَا أُسْتَاذ، الْحِسَاب لَوْ سَمَحْتَ.
lines.en: The juice is really delicious! Excuse me, sir, the bill, please.

lines.ar: لَا، لَا يَا دَانْيَال! الْيَوْم الْحِسَاب عَلَيَّ.
lines.en: No, no, Daniel! Today the bill is on me.

reading.title: Three drinks
reading.ar: الْمَقْهَى قَرِيب مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَة. لَيْلَى تَشْرَبُ قَهْوَةً تُرْكِيَّةً، وَسَامِي يَشْرَبُ شَايًا سَاخِنًا. دَانْيَال يُرِيدُ عَصِيرًا بَارِدًا وَمَاءً.
reading.en: The café is near the school. Layla drinks Turkish coffee, and Sami drinks hot tea. Daniel wants a cold juice and water.

quiz.prompt: How do you say 'please' to a woman?
Which word is the opposite of بَارِد (cold)?
Who pays the bill at the café?
Which sign is the hamza, the little catch in 'uh-oh'?
Complete: 'I'd like a cup of coffee.'

completion: Excellent! You can order drinks politely and say how you like them. Next: dinner at a restaurant.
